tasks.title: Add Account and TransferId fields to Movement
tasks.description: Add to src/modules/models/Movement.model.ts: `Account` (Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref 'Account', required: true), `TransferId` (String, required: false — set only by AccountService.transfer to link a transfer's two generated movements, never client-settable). Mirror both fields in src/modules/interfaces/movement.interface.ts's MovementI (`Account: Types.ObjectId`, `TransferId?: string`). This is a schema-level requirement, not an enforced runtime backfill — existing Movement documents in a real deployed database will still be readable (Mongoose doesn't validate on plain reads), but any create/update without Account will now fail validation. See INT-03 for the migration path.
tasks.notes: Slice 2B (deferred piece of Phase 2). Deviation: Category was also relaxed from required:true to required:false on Movement (model + interface), discovered while implementing INT-04 — AccountService.transfer's two generated movements carry no Category (transfers aren't tied to a spending category) and would otherwise fail Mongoose validation. API-level movement creation is unaffected: movement.validator.ts's isPost rule still requires Category on POST /movement/.

tasks.title: Require Account on movement create, optional on update; keep TransferId system-managed
tasks.description: In src/modules/validators/movement.validator.ts's addUpdateBodyValidate, add Account using the existing isPost pattern already used for Type/Amount/Category: `body('Account').if(isPost).notEmpty().withMessage('Account is required')` + `body('Account').optional().isMongoId().withMessage('Account must be a valid id')`. Add 'Account' to the checkKeys whitelist in paramBodyValidate (`['Type','Amount','Card','Category','Description','Account']`) and to addUpdateBodyValidate's implicit accepted-fields set if there's a separate whitelist call there (check the current file — if addUpdateValidator doesn't call checkKeys today, don't add one; match whatever validation-completeness pattern already exists for Category on that same validator). Deliberately do NOT add 'TransferId' to any whitelist — it must never be settable via POST/PUT /movement, only set internally by AccountService.transfer.
tasks.notes: Slice 2B. Mirrors the isPost pattern already established for Type/Amount/Category on this exact validator. addUpdateBodyValidate does not call checkKeys (confirmed by reading the file), so no whitelist was added there, matching Category's existing treatment. paramBodyValidate's checkKeys whitelist got 'Account' added; TransferId was deliberately excluded from every whitelist. TDD: src/modules/validators/movement.validator.test.ts (new) covers POST-required, MongoId format, and PUT-optional behavior.

tasks.title: Write (but do not run) a migration script to backfill existing movements with a default Account
tasks.description: Create scripts/backfill-movement-accounts.ts, following scripts/hash-password.ts's existing script conventions (reads env, connects via the same MONGO_CONN_STR/MONGO_DB_NAME pattern as src/config/database.ts, runs once, exits). Logic: find-or-create an Account named 'General' (Type: 'efectivo', if one with that Name doesn't already exist); find every Movement document where Account is missing/null; set its Account to the General account's _id via updateMany. Log a summary count of accounts created/movements backfilled. Add an npm script `"backfill-movement-accounts": "ts-node scripts/backfill-movement-accounts.ts"` to package.json, matching the existing hash-password script's wiring. Do NOT execute this script during this task — it mutates a real database and there is no live MongoDB connection available in this session. Document clearly in the script's header comment and in the PR description that this must be run manually against the real database before or immediately after this change is deployed, so existing movements remain writable once Account becomes a required field.
tasks.notes: Slice 2B. Script written with header comment warning it is manual-run only; NOT executed as part of this task — confirmed no `npm run backfill-movement-accounts` invocation occurred. Repo owner must run it manually against the real database around deploy time.

tasks.title: Add AccountService.getBalance and AccountService.transfer
tasks.description: In src/modules/services/account.service.ts add: getBalance(accountId: string): fetch all Movement docs with Account: accountId, sum Amount where Type is 'ingreso' minus sum where Type is 'egreso' (reuse the same find+reduce pattern already used in report.service.ts/budget.service.ts, not a Mongo aggregate pipeline, for consistency), return the net number. transfer(data: { From: string; To: string; Amount: number; Date: Date; Description?: string }): validate From !== To and Amount > 0 at the service layer as a defense-in-depth check (validator will also check this — see INT-05), confirm both From and To resolve to existing, non-archived accounts (404-equivalent error if either doesn't), generate a shared `TransferId` via `new mongoose.Types.ObjectId().toString()`, then create two Movement documents: one Type: 'egreso', Account: From, Amount, Date, Description, TransferId; one Type: 'ingreso', Account: To, Amount, Date, Description, TransferId. Since this project has no MongoDB replica set (no multi-document transactions assumed available — see ONBOARD.md's atomicity note), do NOT use mongoose sessions/transactions. Instead: create the egreso movement first; if the ingreso movement creation then fails, delete the egreso movement you just created (compensating rollback) and rethrow, so a failed transfer never leaves a lone unbalanced movement behind. Return both created movements.
tasks.notes: Slice 2B. report.service.ts does not actually exist in this repo (not yet merged); getBalance's find+reduce style instead mirrors budget.service.ts's getStatus (the closest existing analog). Non-archived check on From/To was initially missed on first pass and added after re-reading this task's acceptance criteria, with dedicated tests (rejects when From/To account is archived). Rollback-on-partial-failure verified by test + manual trace: if the second MovementModel.create() rejects, the catch block calls MovementModel.findByIdAndDelete on the first (egreso) movement's _id before rethrowing the original error — confirmed via a test that mocks the second create() to reject and asserts findByIdAndDelete was called exactly once with the first movement's id. Residual risk (not in scope): if the compensating delete itself fails, that error propagates instead of the original transfer error and the lone egreso movement is not cleaned up — acceptable given no transactions are available, but worth a future improvement (e.g. retry/alerting).

tasks.title: Add GET /account/:id/balance and POST /account/transfer
tasks.description: In src/modules/controllers/account.controller.ts add getAccountBalance (calls AccountService.getBalance, responds { Account: id, Balance }, 404 if the account itself doesn't exist first) and createTransfer (calls AccountService.transfer, responds 201 with the two created movements). In src/modules/validators/account.validator.ts add a transferValidator: body('From').isMongoId(), body('To').isMongoId(), body('Amount').isFloat({ gt: 0 }), body('Date').notEmpty(), body('Description').isString().optional(), plus a custom check that From !== To (400 if equal). Wire into src/modules/routes/account.route.ts: GET /:id/balance (idValidator) — declared BEFORE GET /:id so the literal 'balance' segment under a wildcard resolves correctly (path is /:id/balance, a deeper segment, so it doesn't actually collide with GET /:id — verify this is genuinely safe given Express's routing, since /:id/balance and /:id are different path depths); POST /transfer (transferValidator) — declared BEFORE POST /:id if one existed (there isn't a POST /:id today, so this is safe, but double-check no future :id-shaped POST route would need to come after it).
tasks.notes: Slice 2B. Route ordering confirmed safe by reading the actual route file: GET /:id/balance (2 segments) and GET /:id (1 segment) never collide regardless of order since Express matches by segment count; POST /transfer and POST /:id don't collide either since no POST /:id route exists. transferValidator and GET /:id/balance still placed before the :id-shaped routes for readability/convention consistency.

tasks.title: Add a required Account field to Recurring, and propagate it in run()
tasks.description: Now that Movement.Account is required (INT-01), RecurringService.run()'s MovementModel.create(...) call will fail validation unless the Recurring template also carries an Account. Add `Account` (Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref 'Account', required: true) to src/modules/models/Recurring.model.ts and src/modules/interfaces/recurring.interface.ts. Update src/modules/validators/recurring.validator.ts's isPost-based required fields to include Account (same pattern as Type/Amount/Category/DayOfMonth). Update RecurringService.run() in src/modules/services/recurring.service.ts to pass `Account: recurring.Account` into the MovementModel.create(...) call.
tasks.notes: Slice 2B. REC-01's original notes explicitly deferred adding Account to Recurring until this exact slice landed — this task is that follow-through, not new scope. TDD: src/modules/validators/recurring.validator.test.ts created (none existed before); recurring.service.test.ts's run() assertion updated to expect Account in the created Movement.

tasks.title: Update openapi.yaml for Account/TransferId on Movement, the new balance/transfer endpoints, and Account on Recurring
tasks.description: Update the Movement schema in openapi.yaml to include Account (required) and TransferId (readOnly, optional). Update POST/PUT /movement/ request bodies to include Account (required on POST). Add GET /account/{id}/balance (returns { Account, Balance }) and POST /account/transfer (request: { From, To, Amount, Date, Description }, response: array of the two created Movement objects) to the account paths. Update the Recurring schema to include Account (required) and the POST/PUT /recurring/ request bodies accordingly. All bearerAuth, non-2xx referencing Error. Verify the file still parses with js-yaml after editing (see ONBOARD.md §8 — this file has crashed the server on boot before from a bad merge).
tasks.notes: Slice 2B. Deviation (pre-existing, unrelated to this task's scope but blocking its mandatory parse-verification step): openapi.yaml did NOT parse at all before this change — a duplicate top-level `components:` key had accidentally nested the entire /recurring/* path block inside the first (bogus) components block, and a bad-indentation bug under /budget/'s POST operation (security/requestBody mis-indented under the security list item) threw a YAMLException. Both were fixed: the /recurring/* paths were relocated to their correct place in `paths:`, the two components blocks were merged into one (also recovering Budget/BudgetStatus schemas, which only existed in the deleted first block), and the budget POST indentation was corrected. Verified via `node -e "require('js-yaml').load(...)"` and by actually importing src/config/openapi.ts with ts-node, both succeeding post-fix. Movement schema's `required` list intentionally omits Category (see INT-01 deviation) with a prose note on POST /movement/ clarifying Category is still required by the validator on create.

tasks.title: Tests for the Movement-Account integration
tasks.description: Update movement.controller.test.ts / movement.validator's coverage where needed for the new Account requirement (POST without Account 400s, PUT without Account still succeeds if other fields are valid). Add account.service.test.ts coverage for getBalance (sums ingreso minus egreso correctly across mixed movements) and transfer (creates two linked movements sharing a TransferId; rejects From === To; rejects a non-positive Amount; rolls back the first movement if the second create fails — mock MovementModel.create to reject on the second call and assert a delete/remove call for the first). Add account.controller.test.ts coverage for the two new endpoints. Add recurring coverage confirming run() now includes Account in the created Movement.
tasks.notes: Slice 2B. Full suite green: 155 tests passing (16 test files), `npm run build` clean, `npm run lint` clean. movement.validator.test.ts and recurring.validator.test.ts did not exist before this change and were created from scratch, following the account.validator.test.ts pattern. The transfer rollback-on-partial-failure test is the highest-value case here and was manually traced end-to-end (see INT-04 notes) — it prevents a failed transfer from silently leaving a one-sided movement in the ledger.

tasks.title: Fix AccountService.transfer's errors mapping to 500 instead of 404/400
tasks.description: AccountService.transfer() throws plain Error objects for 6 distinct failure modes; createTransfer's catch calls errorResponse(res, toMessage(error)) with no status argument, defaulting to 500 for all of them — confirmed codified as 'correct' in the staged test (`expect(res.status).toHaveBeenCalledWith(500)` for 'From account not found'). Create src/utils/service-error.util.ts exporting `class ServiceError extends Error { statusCode: number; constructor(message: string, statusCode: number) { super(message); this.statusCode = statusCode; this.name = 'ServiceError'; } }`. In account.service.ts's transfer(), replace each `throw new Error(...)` with `throw new ServiceError(message, statusCode)`: 'From and To accounts must be different' -> 400, 'Amount must be greater than 0' -> 400, 'From account not found' -> 404, 'To account not found' -> 404, 'From account is archived' -> 400, 'To account is archived' -> 400. In account.controller.ts's createTransfer, change the catch to: `const statusCode = error instanceof ServiceError ? error.statusCode : 500; errorResponse(res, toMessage(error), statusCode);`. Update the existing test that asserted 500 for 'From account not found' to assert 404 instead — that assertion was locking in the bug.
tasks.notes: From /code-review findings on slice 2B (5 independent review angles converged on this defect). This introduces the codebase's first typed-error convention — deliberately minimal (one class, one field), not a broader error-hierarchy redesign. Implemented via TDD: updated the existing 500-status test to 404 (confirmed it failed against old code first), added ServiceError, replaced all 6 throw sites, updated controller catch block. Full status-code matrix now covered by tests.

tasks.title: Block TransferId from being client-settable via POST/PUT /movement
tasks.description: movement.validator.ts's addUpdateBodyValidate (used by POST /movement/ and PUT /movement/:id) has no checkKeys whitelist call at all, unlike paramBodyValidate in the same file — so the new TransferId field (meant to be system-managed only, set exclusively by AccountService.transfer) can currently be set directly by any client. Add a checkKeys whitelist to addUpdateBodyValidate matching the fields addUpdateValidator's handler actually processes: ['Type','Amount','Category','Account','Date','Description','Card'] (include 'Date' — addUpdateValidator's handler reads/converts req.body.Date before running these validations, so it's a legitimate accepted field; deliberately exclude 'TransferId'). Verify carefully against the existing test suite that this doesn't reject any field currently accepted by movement create/update — run the full suite and fix any test that was relying on an undocumented extra field.
tasks.notes: From /code-review findings on slice 2B. Chose the general fix (whitelist, matching paramBodyValidate's existing pattern in the same file) over a narrow TransferId-only guard, since the underlying gap (no whitelist at all on this validator) would just resurface for the next sensitive field. Whitelist added exactly as specified: ['Type','Amount','Category','Account','Date','Description','Card']. Full suite (160 tests after adding 3 TransferId-whitelist tests) went green with zero pre-existing test bodies needing changes — no legitimate request shape relied on an undocumented field.

tasks.title: Stop RecurringService.run() from silently losing data on pre-migration Recurring docs missing Account
tasks.description: run() atomically claims a Recurring template (sets LastRunYearMonth) BEFORE creating its Movement. Any Recurring document that predates this slice (created before Account became a field) has no Account, so MovementModel.create() throws a ValidationError AFTER the claim already succeeded — permanently marking that recurring as 'run' for the month with zero Movement created (silent, unrecoverable loss), and the uncaught exception aborts the for-loop, skipping every other due recurring later in iteration order for this invocation too. Fix: (1) before attempting the atomic claim for a given recurring, check `if (!recurring.Account) continue;` — skip it entirely without claiming, so it stays eligible for a correct run() once someone sets its Account via PUT. (2) Wrap the claim-succeeded block (date clamping + MovementModel.create) in its own try/catch so a failure for one recurring (for any reason, not just missing Account) logs (console.error, no logger exists in this codebase) and continues to the next recurring instead of aborting the whole batch.
tasks.notes: From /code-review findings on slice 2B. This is the most severe finding: a real financial-ledger data-loss bug for any pre-existing Recurring templates created before this slice merges, with no migration path (scripts/backfill-movement-accounts.ts only backfills Movement, not Recurring). Implemented the Account guard (skip-without-claiming) and wrapped the post-claim block in try/catch with console.error identifying the recurring id. Two pre-existing test fixtures (in 'running twice in the same month' and 'clamps DayOfMonth' tests) were missing Account and had to be given one — those were an accidental gap (fixtures pre-dated the Account field), not intentional coverage of the missing-Account path, so adding Account: 'acc1' was the correct fix rather than weakening any assertion.

tasks.title: Validate and convert Date in transferBodyValidate
tasks.description: account.validator.ts's transferBodyValidate only does body('Date').notEmpty() — no format validation, no string-to-Date conversion, unlike movement.validator.ts's addUpdateValidator (checkDate + new Date(date)). An invalid date string passes validation and reaches MovementModel.create() inside AccountService.transfer, producing a raw Mongoose CastError that surfaces as an opaque 500 (compounded by INT-09's fix, this would become a 500 from a genuinely unexpected error type rather than a clean 400). Add `.custom(checkDate)` (import from src/utils/validator.util.ts, same helper movement.validator.ts already uses) to the Date rule in transferBodyValidate. In transferValidator's handler, before running the validation chain, convert a string Date to an actual Date object the same way addUpdateValidator does: `if (typeof req.body.Date === 'string' && checkDate(req.body.Date)) { req.body.Date = new Date(req.body.Date); }`.
tasks.notes: From /code-review findings on slice 2B. Implemented exactly per spec: .custom(checkDate) added to the Date rule, and transferValidator's handler mirrors addUpdateValidator's string-to-Date conversion pattern precisely.

tasks.title: Restore Category as required on POST /movement/'s OpenAPI schema
tasks.description: The shared Movement schema's `required` array correctly dropped Category (now [Amount, Date, Type, Account]) to match the Mongoose relaxation, but POST /movement/'s requestBody references this same shared schema with no override — only a non-enforced prose description claims Category is still required on create. Any OpenAPI-driven tooling (Swagger UI request validation, generated client SDKs, contract tests) would treat Category as optional. Change POST /movement/'s requestBody schema to `allOf: [{ $ref: '#/components/schemas/Movement' }, { required: ['Category'] }]` so the machine-readable contract matches movement.validator.ts's actual isPost rule.
tasks.notes: From /code-review findings on slice 2B — user explicitly asked to verify openapi.yaml alignment with the actual project behavior. Implemented exactly as specified (allOf + required: ['Category']). openapi.yaml verified to still parse via js-yaml after the edit.

tasks.title: Fix POST /account/transfer's OpenAPI description overclaiming the rollback guarantee
tasks.description: The description states the compensating rollback means 'a failed transfer never leaves a lone unbalanced movement behind' — but the rollback's own MovementModel.findByIdAndDelete call was unguarded (see INT-16) and can itself fail, leaving an orphaned movement despite the doc's absolute wording. Reword to describe best-effort compensation rather than an unconditional guarantee, e.g.: 'On failure creating the second movement, the service attempts to delete the first as a best-effort compensation — this is not a database transaction, so in rare cases (e.g. the compensating delete itself fails) a single unbalanced movement may remain and require manual reconciliation.'
tasks.notes: From /code-review findings on slice 2B — user explicitly asked to verify openapi.yaml alignment with the actual project behavior. Implemented after INT-16 so the wording accurately reflects real behavior (best-effort compensation, original error logged and re-thrown on rollback failure). openapi.yaml verified to still parse via js-yaml after the edit.

tasks.title: Use TypeMovement.INGRESO enum instead of the raw string literal in getBalance
tasks.description: AccountService.getBalance() compares movement.Type === 'ingreso' as a raw string literal, even though this same file already imports TypeMovement and correctly uses TypeMovement.EGRESO/TypeMovement.INGRESO a few lines later in transfer(). Change the comparison to use the enum for consistency and rename-safety.
tasks.notes: From /code-review findings on slice 2B (flagged independently by 2 review angles). Verified TypeMovement.INGRESO === 'ingreso' before refactoring (value-equivalent change). Pre-existing account.service.test.ts coverage for getBalance (mixed ingreso/egreso) already exercises this branch and continued passing — no new test needed per the task's own guidance.

tasks.title: Log (don't silently mask) a failed compensating rollback in transfer()
tasks.description: The compensating rollback (MovementModel.findByIdAndDelete on the egreso movement, when the ingreso create fails) has no error handling of its own — if the delete itself throws, its error replaces the original transfer failure in what the caller sees, and there is no trace anywhere that a real-money egreso movement is now orphaned. Wrap the delete in its own try/catch: on failure, console.error a structured message identifying the orphaned movement id and TransferId (no logger exists in this codebase to use instead), then re-throw the ORIGINAL error (not the rollback's error) so the caller still sees the real cause.
tasks.notes: From /code-review findings on slice 2B. Implemented as specified: compensating delete wrapped in its own try/catch, console.error logs the orphaned movement id and TransferId on rollback failure, original error is re-thrown (verified via a test asserting error identity, not just message equality).
